clue.text: One or two in the cricket team?

definitions.text: One or two in the cricket team?

parts.words: One or two in the cricket team?
parts.note: a cricket side sends out a pair of batsmen to start its innings, so either of that pair fits the description

explanation.surface: A vague question about how many players are in a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two' reads like a headcount, but it means either of the two batsmen who begin a cricket innings.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the two batsmen who start the innings are each called by this title, being first to face the bowling.

clue.text: Calm down situation after invasion of revolutionary army

indicators.note: after invasion of says the situation word has been entered by the army letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: a situation is a place or position

indicators.note: revolutionary means the army's letters turn right round

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Restoring order to a situation after a rebel army invades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' here means turned round, not rebellious; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or appease someone is to soothe their anger, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Anything but an old-fashioned rocker, it's observed

parts.note: anything but, as a retort, is a flat refusal or denial
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a person is far from being an old rocker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy (Ted) was a 1950s British rock-and-roll fan in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noted has been remarked upon or seen, so observed is a synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Bishop in wobble with hero in defiance

indicators.note: in places the bishop's letter inside the wobble word

parts.note: to reel is to stagger or wobble
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a lion is a brave hero, as in a literary lion or a lionheart

explanation.surface: A bishop shakily stands alongside a hero in an act of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Open defiance of authority, an uprising, is what a revolt amounts to.

clue.text: Birds going around quarry where flying must be controlled

indicators.note: going around says the bird word encircles the quarry word

parts.note: cocks are male birds
a pit is a quarry or excavation

explanation.surface: Birds circling over a quarry, in a place where flight is regulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' and 'flying' suggest the definition is about birds; it is the pilot's compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilot's compartment of an aircraft is the place from which the plane is flown.

clue.text: Repeatedly take care of teachers' organisation, one taking a hit?

indicators.note: repeatedly says that abbreviation appears twice in a row

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain

explanation.surface: A teachers' union keeps having to look after a member who has been struck.
explanation.walkthrough: At a coconut shy, a British fairground stall, people throw balls to knock these off their stands.
explanation.definitionFit: At a fairground shy the target nuts are struck by thrown balls, so each is something taking a hit.

clue.text: Conservative sitting on grass making dogmatic statement

indicators.note: sitting on places the first letter above the grass word in this down entry

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A Tory perched on the lawn delivering a doctrinaire pronouncement.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a formal statement of belief, a fixed set of tenets held dogmatically.

clue.text: Sniping at terrible pieces of art

indicators.note: terrible says the letters are in a dreadful state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A critic taking potshots at some dreadful artworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Works on canvas made with brush and pigment are examples of artworks.

clue.text: Heavy drinker in street turning up to see films

indicators.note: in puts the drinker inside the street letters
turning up in a down entry means the street letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an alkie is slang for an alcoholic

explanation.surface: A drunk wandering up the road on the way to the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turning up' reads the street abbreviation from the bottom, giving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Early films with soundtracks were called by this name, an informal term for movies.

clue.text: Like a drug that's intricate a lab developed

indicators.note: developed says the letters have been worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: A complex medicine produced in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that kills germs is described this way, so the adjective fits a medicine like penicillin.

clue.text: Instrument fellow going to party left at home

indicators.note: going to says the fellow word is followed by the party word

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a do is an informal party
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man heading to a party but leaving his instrument behind at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute-like stringed instrument played with a plectrum is an example of an instrument.

clue.text: Particular ending comes after editor's made reversal

indicators.note: comes after places the ending word behind the reversed letters
made reversal says the editor's letters turn backwards

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
a tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: An editor backtracks so that a particular conclusion follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is an individual item or point, the noun sense of a fine point.

clue.text: Stars saving time get small car

indicators.note: saving here means except, so the word get loses the time letter

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: Celebrities who economise on time by buying a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means except: GET without T leaves GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins constellation is a group of stars, the third sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Aim to be under shelter, the first thing after upset

indicators.note: after places the reversed letters behind the shelter phrase

parts.note: being in a tent puts you under shelter

indicators.note: upset in a down entry says those letters are turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: number one, written NO I, is the first thing

explanation.surface: A plan to get under cover, the first priority after an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first thing' is No. 1, written NOI; 'upset' reverses it to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose or goal you mean to achieve is your aim, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Spooner's to identify tragic female indicating lack of spirit

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words swap places

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine

explanation.surface: Pointing out a doomed heroine as an example of meekness.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of NAME and TESS gives TAME NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Docility or meekness is a want of fire or spirit, as in an animal that has been domesticated.

clue.text: Learners caught in fine rain with one load hard to bear

indicators.note: caught in says the learners sit inside the rain word

parts.note: mist is a fine drizzle
L is a learner driver, so two learners are LL

explanation.surface: Learner drivers stuck in drizzle with a heavy burden to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy burden or encumbrance, from the idiom of a weight round your neck.

clue.text: Argues as one opposing nurses

parts.note: a con is an argument or voter against, as in pros and cons
to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: Someone opposing nurses in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning cares for.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain or assert a view in debate is to argue it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Senior citizen courageous, but no leader, endlessly severe

indicators.note: no leader says the courageous word loses its first letter

parts.note: bold means courageous

indicators.note: endlessly says the severe word loses its last letter

parts.note: stern means severe

explanation.surface: An old person who is brave but harsh, though no longer in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person, an elderly member of society, informally described.

clue.text: Employee in group outside front of restaurant with vehicle

indicators.note: outside says the group word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of restaurant

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A staff member among a crowd outside a restaurant with a van.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works for another, especially in a household, is a kind of employee.

clue.text: Belittle some tales — 'sentimental'

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sneering at stories for being soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish or reduce the importance of something is to make it smaller, as belittling does.

clue.text: English sermon troubled American writer

indicators.note: troubled says the sermon's letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A preacher's English sermon unsettling an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges SERMON into MERSON. Ralph Waldo Emerson was a 19th-century American essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo, the Transcendentalist essayist and poet, is a famous example of a US author.

clue.text: A daughter getting on is one who looks good

indicators.note: getting says the daughter letter is followed by the next word

explanation.surface: An ageing daughter who is still a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word, but its letters end the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The handsome youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth gave his name to any strikingly attractive man.

clue.text: Woman starts to decorate expensive material

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: A woman beginning to decorate with costly fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather with a napped surface is an example of a material used for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Tried again after faulty start, being shy

definitions.meaning: in tennis a player who faults on a first serve has to put the ball into play once more

explanation.surface: A tennis player taking a second serve after a fault, too timid to show it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SERVED, it is what a tennis player does after a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person who keeps feelings to themselves is described with this adjective, a synonym for shy.

clue.text: Feature of stairs concerning gentleman ascending

indicators.note: ascending in a down entry says both pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
sir is a title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Something about a gentleman climbing a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascending' reverses RE + SIR as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical board between two steps is a part of every staircase.

clue.text: Dinosaurs creating difficulty for top careerists

indicators.note: creating difficulty for says the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned fogeys making trouble for ambitious high-flyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating difficulty for' rearranges TOP CAREERISTS. 'Dinosaurs' could mean old fogeys, but here they are the real three-horned beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-horned herbivores of the late Cretaceous are an example of the extinct reptiles.

clue.text: Intricate patterns in one part of church

indicators.note: intricate says the letters are complicated into a new order

explanation.surface: Elaborate decorations in one area of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-arm of a cruciform church building is one of its parts, crossing the nave.

clue.text: Monarch to rave, going off course

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
to rant is to rave

explanation.surface: A king or queen ranting and losing direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering or straying from the right path, as a knight-errant roams; a straying adjective.
